units: <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 52">Pirké d’R. El. ch. LII</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 927:7">Yalk. Job 927</cite> <he>לא נמצא אדם עוֹטֵשׁ וחיה וכ׳</he> (up to Jacob’s days) it had never occurred that a man sneezed and recovered from his sickness. Y’lamd. to Gen. XXVII, quot. in Ar. <he>אדם עוטש אומר לו וכ׳</he> when a person sneezes, one says to him, Good life!—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:5:17">Y. Ber. III, 6ᵈ</cite> bot.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: <cite ref="P00484">same</cite>. Ib. <he>אני … מפהק ומְעַטֵּשׁ</he> I saw him yawn and sneeze.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 9:8">Nidd. IX, 8</cite> <he>מפהקת ומְעַטֶּשֶׁת</he> she yawns and sneezes (or feels inflated; symptoms of approaching menstruation); a. fr.

senses.gloss: <cite ref="P00484">same</cite>. Yalk. Job l. c. <he>לפיכך … כשמִתְעַטֵּשׁ</he> therefore one must offer thanks when one sneezes.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:21">Num. R. s. 9</cite> <he>תהא מִתְעַטֶּשֶׁת וכ׳</he> she will feel inflated and languid. Y. Succ. V, 55ᵇ bot. <he>היו מִתְעַטְּשׁוֹת מריח וכ׳</he> used to sneeze on account of the smell of the frankincense (offered at the Temple); a. fr.
